newsitem.title: INDIA: Cyclone nears India's southeast coast.
newsitem.headline: Cyclone nears India's southeast coast.

text.p: A cyclone bearing down on India's southeastern state of Andhra Pradesh is likely to hit the coast early on Wednesday, meteorological officials said.
The storm was 500 km (344 miles) east southeast of the coastal town of Machilipatnam early on Tuesday, the India Meteorological Department said in a statement.
It was likely to cross the coast in the early hours of Wednesday, the statement added.
Gale force winds of 70-90 kph (44-55 mph) and rough seas were expected to start battering the coast on Tuesday afternoon, it said.
The state relief commissioner, H.S. Brahma, said cyclone warnings had been issued and fishermen had been advised not to put out to sea.
"We have evacuated about 15,000 people from low-lying areas in the coast," Brahma told Reuters by phone from the state capital of Hyderabad.
"Our problem is that at the moment, we are not sure where the cyclone will hit," he said. "It is moving slowly and we are keeping our fingers crossed."
The state was devastated last month by a severe storm in which more than 2,000 people were killed or were missing at sea. Property damage was estimated at more than 50 billion rupees ($1.4 billion).
